name: Interpolation Methods
text:
# Interpolation Methods

Also called: Interpolation Schemes

## Overview
Interpolation methods reconstruct a continuous scalar field from discrete voxel data to evaluate density or opacity at arbitrary query positions along viewing rays [G]. This family solves the problem of discretization artifacts (aliasing, blockiness) inherent in nearest-neighbor sampling while balancing computational cost against spatial smoothness [S2, unofficial][S3, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from sibling techniques like [Sampling and Jittering](2516-sampling-and-jittering.md) by focusing on the spatial reconstruction kernel rather than the temporal or positional jittering of sample points, and from [Gradient-Based Interpolation by Sample Splatting](9072-gradient-based-interpolation-by-sample-splatting.md) by typically operating directly on the voxel grid rather than sparse sample splats.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family map a query position $\mathbf{p}$ in [voxel space](#3074-voxel-space.md) to a scalar value $V(\mathbf{p})$ by combining a finite set of neighboring voxel values $V_i$ using a set of weights $w_i(\mathbf{p})$:
$$
V(\mathbf{p}) = \sum_{i} w_i(\mathbf{p}) V_i
$$
The weights are derived from a reconstruction kernel $h(\mathbf{z})$, where $\mathbf{z}$ is the distance from the query point to the sample center [G]. The choice of kernel defines the trade-off between computational complexity, spatial extent (number of neighbors), and frequency response (aliasing vs. blurring) [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Interpolation Schemes for Volume Rendering](817-interpolation-schemes-for-volume-rendering.md)
Standard schemes (e.g., Trilinear, Lanczos) that reconstruct the field directly from voxel data. Choose when high-quality, smooth reconstruction of the scalar field is required without auxiliary data structures.

### [Gradient-Based Interpolation by Sample Splatting](9072-gradient-based-interpolation-by-sample-splatting.md)
Uses gradients and [splatting](#23-splatting.md) for radiance interpolation. Choose for inhomogeneous media with sharp shading variations (light shafts) where standard [voxel interpolation](#6486-voxel-interpolation-nearest-trilinear-triquadratic-tricubic.md) fails.

### [Shape-Based Interpolation](10499-shape-based-interpolation.md)
Preserves geometric boundaries by interpolating a scene representation. Choose for surface rendering where edge integrity is critical.

### [Lanczos Resampling](11246-lanczos-resampling.md)
Windowed [sinc interpolation](#2085-ideal-low-pass-filter-rect-filter.md). Choose when sharper frequency response and reduced aliasing are needed compared to linear/cubic methods, accepting higher computational cost.

### Joseph's Method
A forward [projection method](#8336-projection-method.md) for 2D easily extended to 3D, using bi-linear interpolation on intersection points and a compensation factor for rays deviating from the principal direction [S2, unofficial]. It determines the principal direction by comparing absolute differences $|x_1-x_2|$, $|y_1-y_2|$, and $|z_1-z_2|$ [S2, unofficial]. For the case where the x-axis is principal, it performs bi-linear interpolation on the intersection points of each $(y, z)$-plane [S2, unofficial]. The sum of interpolations is weighted by $\frac{\sqrt{(x_1 - x_2)^2 + (y_1 - y_2)^2 + (z_1 - z_2)^2}}{|x_1 - x_2|}$ to compensate for longer traversal [S2, unofficial]. It performs similarly to Köhler's method in accuracy despite using a skewed kernel [S2, unofficial].

### Interblock Interpolation
A technique to handle missing samples between blocks by interpolating from neighbors, allowing for higher data reduction [S3, unofficial]. The interpolated value is a normalized sum, $\phi$, of bounded block samples, $\phi_b$ [S3, unofficial]. It enables data reduction of 80:1 (1.25% of original size) or 40:1 to 50:1 (2% of original size) [S3, unofficial].

### Higher-Order Interpolation via Template
An extension of [template-based ray casting](#7802-ray-template-traversal.md) that uses connected cells instead of connected voxels to support higher-order interpolation by taking multiple samples along continuous rays within each cell [S4, unofficial]. It takes multiple samples at regular intervals along the continuous ray inside each cell and precomputes part of the interpolation function in a table for faster rendering [S4, unofficial].

### Nearest Neighbor Sampling
A [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) interpolation technique that selects the closest sample point to the ray's current position when the ray does not land exactly on a sample grid point [S5, unofficial]. It produces lower quality images compared to trilinear interpolation but requires less execution time [S5, unofficial].

## Background
Interpolation is fundamental to volume rendering, addressing the mismatch between discrete voxel grids and continuous viewing rays. Early methods like Nearest Neighbor and Trilinear Interpolation were standard for their simplicity and speed [S1, unofficial][S5, unofficial]. Forward projection methods like Joseph's Method (1982) and Köhler's method (2000) were developed to improve accuracy in projection-based rendering [S2, unofficial]. Advanced techniques like Interblock Interpolation (Hadwiger et al.) emerged to support extreme data reduction in GPU-based rendering [S3, unofficial]. Template-based higher-order interpolation expanded on these principles for specific rendering pipelines [S4, unofficial].
